comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom disclose active securities class action lawsuits alleging violations of federal securities laws regarding misleading statements. Intel's lawsuit focuses on the growth prospects of its foundry business following a segment reporting change, with a motion to dismiss filed in December 2024. Broadcom's lawsuit concerns VMware's backlog statements; while filed in 2020, the motion to dismiss was denied in April 2023, and the parties agreed to settlement terms pending court approval in 2024. Unlike Intel's case which is at the motion to dismiss stage, Broadcom's is at a settlement negotiation stage.

sentences.text: A securities class action lawsuit was filed in the US District Court for the Northern District of California in May 2024 against us and certain officers following the modification of our segment reporting in the first quarter of 2024 to align to our new internal foundry operating model.
We filed a motion to dismiss the amended consolidated complaint in December 2024.

On September 18, 2020, the plaintiffs filed a consolidated amended complaint alleging that VMware's statements about backlog and the related internal controls during the period from August 2018 through February 2020 were materially misleading.
The defendants' motion to dismiss the Second Amended Consolidated Complaint was filed on November 5, 2021.
